title: Register copy run
statement: Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $h$ be a Boolean word. Choose a stage $s$ among eight stages and let $v$ assign each of the fourteen registers a natural number at most $B$. Suppose the source register specified by stage $s$ is at most the destination register specified by that stage. Then the abstract machine, starting in the copy state for stage $s$ with its bump flag false, register assignment $v$, and no recorded answer, reaches the state prescribed by that stage with the destination register set to the original source-register value and every other register unchanged; throughout the run, the prescribed configuration invariant holds.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$s$ is one of eight copy stages
$v$ assigns each of fourteen registers a natural number at most $B$
the source register specified by $s$ has value at most that of the destination register specified by $s$

assignment $v$. If every register value is at most $B$ and the source register specified
by stage $s$ is no larger than its destination register, then the machine reaches the
state prescribed by stage $s$, with the destination register replaced by the source
register’s original value and all other registers unchanged, starting from the copy
